articles.title: Find anything on any website

body.support:
Websites look different. But most have the same parts in the same places.

**At the top**

- **Logo:** click it to go back to the **home page**.
- **Menu:** the main sections. On a phone, tap the **three lines** (☰).
- **Search bar:** type what you want.

**In the middle**

- **Headings:** what each part is about.
- **Links and buttons:** click them to go somewhere.

**At the bottom: the footer**

- **Contact us:** phone and email.
- **About us:** who runs the site.
- **Privacy.**

**Read the web address.**

- **.gov.au** means government.
- **.edu.au** means a school or TAFE.
- **.com** usually means a business.

Fake sites copy real ones. Check the address!

**Tricky words.** *Apply*, *application*. *Eligible* means allowed to.
body.core:
Websites look different, but most are built from the same parts, in the same places. Once you know them, you can find your way around almost any site.

**At the top**

- **Logo:** usually top left. Click it to go back to the **home page**.
- **Menu:** the main sections, like *Services*, *Jobs* or *About*. On a phone, the menu is often hidden under **three lines** (☰).
- **Search bar:** a box with a magnifying glass. Use it when you know exactly what you want.

**In the middle**

- **Breadcrumbs:** a trail like *Home > Jobs > Apprenticeships*. It shows where you are. Click any part to go back.
- **Headings:** tell you what each section is about.
- **Links and buttons:** blue or underlined words, or buttons like *Apply now*.

**At the bottom: the footer**

- **Contact us:** phone numbers, emails and addresses.
- **About us:** who runs the site.
- **Privacy** and **accessibility**: what they do with your information, and how they help people with disability use the site.

**Read the web address.** The **web address** (URL) tells you a lot:

- **.gov.au**: an Australian government site.
- **.edu.au**: a school, TAFE or university.
- **.org.au**: often a charity or community group.
- **.com.au** or **.com**: usually a business.

Fake sites sometimes copy a real site's look. Check the address carefully: *mygov-help.com* is not *my.gov.au*.

**Tricky words in menus.** Websites use formal words. Break them into parts or use word families: *eligibility* (*eligible*: allowed to), *application* (*apply*), *concession* (a discount).
body.extend:
Websites look different, but most follow the same layout rules. Once you know them, you can find your way around a new site quickly.

**Header**

- **Logo:** usually top left. It links to the **home page**.
- **Menu:** the main sections. On a phone, it's often hidden behind a **hamburger icon** (☰).
- **Search:** best when you know exactly what you need.

**Body**

- **Breadcrumbs** (*Home > Jobs > Apprenticeships*) show where you are in the site. You can click back up.
- **Headings** organise the page. Buttons like *Apply now* or *Book a test* lead to tasks.

**Footer**

The footer holds **contact** details, **about** information, and the **privacy**, **terms** and **accessibility** pages.

**Domains and trust.** The **domain** shows who runs a site. **.gov.au** means an Australian government. **.edu.au** means a school, TAFE or university. **.org.au** is often a not-for-profit. **.com.au** and **.com** are usually businesses. Fake sites can copy a real site's design, so check the full address, not just the look.

**Formal words.** Government sites use formal language. Use word families to decode it: *eligibility* comes from *eligible* (allowed to); *application* comes from *apply*; a *concession* is a lower price.

caseStudies.title: From 900 websites to one design

body.support:
Imagine searching hundreds of different websites to find one thing. Each one looks different.

That was a problem in Victoria. In **2015**, one government department had **36** different websites. Across Victoria, there were more than **900** government web addresses.

So the government made one shared design. The main site is **vic.gov.au**.

Now lots of government sites look and work the same way. Same menu. Same search. Same footer. People can find things faster.

Today, more than **60** websites use it.

Good design helps people find what they need.
body.core:
Imagine needing something from the Victorian Government, and having to search through hundreds of different websites. Each one looks different. The menu is in a different place. The search works differently.

That was the problem Victoria faced. The government's digital team looked into it. In **2015**, one department alone ran **36** different websites. Each had its own look and system. Across Victoria, there were more than **900** web addresses ending in *vic.gov.au*.

So the government started building a **Single Digital Presence**: one shared platform and design for government websites. The main site is **vic.gov.au**.

The idea is simple. If every government site uses the same layout, people find things faster. The header, menu, search and footer are always in the same place. People don't have to learn a new website every time.

Today, the government says more than **60** websites use the shared platform, and **vic.gov.au** has more than **120** sections from all 10 government departments.

The lesson: good website design isn't just about looking nice. It's about helping people find things, especially the things they really need.
body.extend:
Imagine trying to use government services spread across hundreds of websites. Each has its own menus, search and layout.

That was Victoria's situation. The government's digital team found that in **2015**, a single department ran **36** websites, with different branding and systems. Across the state, there were more than **900** vic.gov.au web addresses.

The answer was the **Single Digital Presence**: one shared platform and design for government websites, built around **vic.gov.au**.

The key idea is consistency. When sites share the same header, menu, search, headings and footer, people don't have to relearn each one. They find information and services faster.

The government now says more than **60** websites use the platform, and **vic.gov.au** has more than **120** sections from all 10 government departments.

The case shows that web design is really about usability: helping people find what they need, quickly and with confidence.

teacher.overview: Students learn the shared layout of websites (logo and home, menu and hamburger icon, search, breadcrumbs, headings and calls to action, and the footer with contact, about, privacy and accessibility), how to read a web address and domain to judge who runs a site, and how to decode formal interface vocabulary. They annotate a web page, sort where to go for tasks, interpret web addresses, and tour a real site, guiding a partner to one find. The case study is Victoria's Single Digital Presence: after finding more than 900 vic.gov.au web addresses and 36 websites in one department in 2015, the government moved many sites onto one shared design centred on vic.gov.au.

teacher.answers:
**Check your reading:** e.g. logo (top left), menu (top), search (top right), breadcrumbs (under the menu), footer (bottom). When you know exactly what you want. It's an Australian government site; fake sites copy the look of real ones.

**Web page:** 1 logo (home); 2 menu; 3 search; 4 breadcrumbs; 5 heading and call-to-action button; 6 footer with contact, about, privacy, accessibility and a .gov.au address.

**Sort:** phone number — footer; hard rubbish form — search; all services — menu; privacy — footer; skate park hours — search; sport and recreation — menu.

**Addresses:** Youth Central — Victorian Government, yes; Chisholm — a TAFE (.edu.au), yes for course info; Bunnings — a business, for product info; mygov-account-help.com — not the government (.com, copies the name): don't trust it.

realityCheck: **Students are fast on phones but miss footers.** Make the footer the first stop for contact details.
**Never visit real scam sites in class.** Use made-up addresses.
**Guiding a partner is the real test.** It shows they understand the layout, not just luck.
**Works in a real class:** yes. Quick, practical and immediately useful.
